messages:
nate_r: Heads-up: Starting work on identity rationalization for traces/metrics. Goal: unify service_id, svc_key, and vendor_id into a single `canonical_service` while keeping billing stable. Posting proposed rollback/safety guards for review.

geeta_p: Important we treat traces and metrics slightly differently. Traces rely on identity for sampling buckets; metrics are used directly in billing. Suggest explicit propagation flags.

hannah_l: Agree. Also: any change that affects cardinality can blow up our query cost. Need an immediate budget throttle on backfill jobs.

chun: Quick list of potential failure modes I worry about:
- inadvertent ID collisions causing aggregated spikes
- dashboards failing when joins use missing canonical key
- billing drift during partial backfills
- enrichment service becoming hot spot and introducing tail latency

nate_r: Good list. Proposed safeguards: dual-tag pattern, query-time aliasing, staged backfill with dry-run diffs, and per-job rate caps. Details below.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Started canary job group: identity-rationalize-canary-1 (25 shards). Status: running.

geeta_p: Dual-tag pattern = keep original fields and add `canonical_service` + `id_origin` tag so consumers can opt-in. TTL of original fields 45d by default.

hannah_l: For query aliasing, prefer a lightweight resolver cache service instead of touching many SQLs. Resolver should accept legacy key and return canonical or list of aliases. Cache TTL 5m, refresh async.

chun: Backfill plan idea:
1) Dry-run pass that computes attribution diffs (no writes).
2) If diffs < 0.2% for billing buckets and <1% for top-100 dashboards, proceed.
3) Run backfill in micro-batches (1h windows), throttled to <5% of ingestion RPS.
4) Monitor synthetic assertions and abort on any spike >2x baseline or billing delta >0.5%.

nate_r: Additions: every backfill job records a snapshot manifest (shard, time-range, checksums). Jobs must be idempotent and include resume tokens. Also run a shadow join test: feed canonical keys into a sidecar query and compare rollups to live dashboards for 1h window before commit.

geeta_p: For sampling: ensure trace sampler keys are derived from legacy id until resolver is read-consistent. Otherwise we risk splitting traces across buckets. Sampler config should be feature-flagged and staged per region.

hannah_l: Storage concerns: canonical mapping table could be large. Use compact encoding and TTL on mappings older than 90d unless a tenant opts for longer retention. Consider sharded range lookups to avoid hot partitions.

chun: Observability checks to create now:
- hourly billing-diff job for top 500 tenants (calc delta pre/post)
- alert if resolver 99.9th latency > 100ms or error rate > 0.1%
- dashboard diffs for top-200 services with count/latency variance threshold of 1%

nate_r: Rollout flags and rollback knobs:
- obs-proxy: `canonical_id_write_pct` (0..100)
- query-layer: `alias_resolver_enabled` (bool) and `alias_precedence` (string: canonical|legacy)
- backfill: `max_rps_pct` and `dry_run`

Command to flip obs-proxy write pct (example):
```
# set canonical writes to 10%
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://config.internal/v1/flags/obs-proxy/canonical_id_write_pct --data '{"pct":10}'
```

chun: Rollback criteria (auto + manual):
- Auto rollback triggers: resolver errors >0.5% sustained for 5m OR billing delta >0.8% for any monitored tenant OR backfill job error rate >1%
- Manual rollback: any unexplained dashboard outage, or high cardinality alert from query cost monitor.

geeta_p: Who owns what? I propose: edge/ingest team (nate_r) owns dual-write and feature flag, infra/query (chun) owns resolver and aliasing, billing (hannah_l) owns diff checks and thresholds. Ops-bot will manage canary jobs.

hannah_l: I'll write the billing-diff runbook and include a preflight checklist: service whitelist, top-k dashboards, tenant budget caps, contact escalation matrix.

nate_r: I'll implement the dual-write with a toggle and add a `X-Canonical-Candidate` header for SDK/local replays so we can test clients without changing production attribution.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Canary job group identity-rationalize-canary-1 completed dry-run. Diff summary: billing delta median 0.03%, 99th 0.18% — within thresholds.

chun: After dry-run pass, we'll enable alias resolver in read-path for a subset of queries (route=canary). Keep resolver in fallback-only mode initially (only used when canonical missing).

geeta_p: Add synthetic that replays 1% of traffic with canonical flag set and checks for span continuity and sampler stability.

hannah_l: One more: ensure billing envelopes carry both ids until retirement window ends. Don't let any downstream consumer drop legacy id until retire date is announced.

nate_r: Retirement timeline proposal: 0-14d canary ramp dual-write; 14-45d ramp backfill and resolver; 45-90d monitor and reduce legacy writes; 90d retire legacy fields (unless opt-out requested).

chun: We'll also add a safety net query that uses legacy keys to reconstruct counts in case of investigation; keep it for 120d.

geeta_p: Sounds good. I'll create the PR checklist and add required tests: will include conflict tests for id collisions, resolver failure injection, and backfill resume tests.

nate_r: Ok. Next sync tomorrow 9am PT. If anyone sees a missing guard or a scenario I didn't think of ping me here. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: identity-rationalize follow-up meeting tomorrow 09:00 PT.

# end of thread
